items.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: Like Miles never seemed to be happy with what he was doing

ctx.x: So you’re thirty now, let’s see, you’ll be a veteran jazz musician in your seventies when it’s two thousand— I can’t do this math. I’m just wondering, where is jazz going to be in thirty years. Because when you look at the history of jazz it’s moved so fast. Sometimes I feel it moves too fast for its own good you know. Like Miles never seemed to be happy with what he was doing and the audience would just catch up with him and then he’d be somewhere else.
Well it’s hard to say what’s going to happen with jazz, but whatever happens, I just hope I’m in the middle of it. That’s the main thing.
